title: Prioritization vs zero-rating: Discrimination on the internet
summary_en: Should internet service providers be allowed to 'zero-rate' specific content (e.g., not count it against data caps), or must they treat all data equally under net-neutrality rules? Gautier and Somogyi compare prioritisation regimes (paid fast lanes) with zero-rating regimes and identify when each produces more — or less — diversity in the content available to consumers, and which regime delivers higher consumer surplus. The paper provides the welfare comparison the net-neutrality debate has often lacked.
data_used: Theoretical paper in industrial organisation. No primary dataset; the analysis is a multi-sided market model with ISPs, content providers and consumers.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for Hungarian and EU telecom regulation (NMHH, BEREC): supports the case that net-neutrality rules forbidding both prioritisation and zero-rating are not always welfare-maximising — under the parameter conditions the paper characterises, allowing zero-rating dominates pure neutrality. Practical input for ongoing BEREC reviews of zero-rating practice in EU broadband markets.
